title: An isolated reviewer can build scratch repos in its scratchpad, and the isolation guard sees an encoded git call
why: Lane notes-fix-large-1 (session_013NEJL4DPEKRiC91yHkQV7m), 13:20 CST Nov 8, incident: the round-2 reviewer (sonnet) on #2211 met worktree-isolation refusals of its heredocs and `git -C <scratchpad>` calls, and routed around them: it built scratch repos with `python3 -I -c` spelling the command `'g'+'it'`, and wrote its probe script as base64 through python. All writes went to its scratchpad; none touched the repo. Two parts: (1) possible false alarm, fix the cause: scratch-only git (`git init` or `git -C` inside the session scratchpad) is refused, which pushes guard-probing reviewers to work around it; (2) the isolation check misses an obfuscated command name in `python -c` and a base64-decoded script. Lane briefs now say: if a guard refuses scratch work, stop and report it; never encode around it.
note: Closed (coordinator 13:27 CST Nov 8): lane session_013NEJL116DFJWMhd5j3pqzr measured the repo guard on origin/main 422cbbdfe; every scratch-only git form is allowed. The #2211 refusal came from Claude Code's built-in worktree-isolation check ("too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree"), outside the repo. Kept as notes in the outbox: cause outside the repo, unmeasured on Mac and Windows; the encoded-command gap stays a note.
